title: Greetings & Introductions
subtitle: Say hello, introduce yourself, and ask how someone is.
objectives: Greet someone correctly for the time of day

content.intro: These are the very first words most people learn in a new language. Practice saying them out loud, not just reading them.

rules.heading: Greetings by time of day
rules.body:
• Good morning — before 12:00 (noon)
  • Good afternoon — 12:00 to about 18:00 (6pm)
  • Good evening — after about 18:00
  • Hello / Hi — any time of day (Hi is more informal)
  • Good night — only when leaving, never as a greeting when you arrive

rules.heading: Introducing yourself
rules.body:
• My name is [name].
  • I'm [name]. (short for "I am")
  • Nice to meet you! — Nice to meet you, too!

rules.heading: How are you?
rules.body:
• How are you? — I'm fine, thank you. And you?
  • How are you doing? — Pretty good, thanks!

examples: Good morning! My name is Carlos.
Hi! I'm Ana. Nice to meet you.
How are you? — I'm fine, thank you. And you?
Good evening! How are you doing?

commonMistakes.wrong: Good night! (when arriving at a party in the evening)
commonMistakes.why: "Good night" is only used when leaving or going to sleep — never as a greeting.
English uses the verb "to be" for age, not "have" — this is a common mix-up from Portuguese ("Eu tenho 25 anos").
"To be" changes to "is" for he/she/it (and for "my name").

exercises.title: Match the Greeting to the Reply

items.explanation: Each greeting has a natural, standard reply in English.

items.prompt: It's 9:00 in the morning. What do you say?
It's 8:00 in the evening, and you're arriving at a friend's house. What do you say?
items.explanation: "Good night" is only for leaving, not arriving — use "Good evening."

items.prompt: Someone asks "How are you?" What is a natural reply?
items.explanation: "I'm fine, thank you" is the standard, natural reply.
A fixed expression: Nice to meet you.

summary: Good morning/afternoon/evening change with the time of day; hello/hi work any time.
"Good night" is only a goodbye, never a greeting.
My name is... / I'm... are the two standard ways to introduce yourself.
How are you? → I'm fine, thank you. And you?
